subject: Models could not be estimated error

messages.author: 11f232522ba7c0f7
messages.subject: Models could not be estimated error
parts:
Hi tidyLPA team,

First of all, thanks so much for the time you have spent developing this package!

Unfortunately, I seem to have run into something that might be a problem and, since I don’t have prior experience with latent profile analysis, I’m not sure how to proceed.  Models with equal variances (models 1 and 3) seem to mostly work fine, but whenever I ask the package to estimate profiles using a model with varying variances (models 2 or 6), it doesn’t work at all.  The package prints this error message:

Error in estimate_profiles(SSP_LPA, Tactile_Sensitivity, Taste_Smell_Sensitivity,  : 
  Model could not be estimated.

Is this a problem, and if so, do you have any idea why it might be occurring?  Our data are scores on the Short Sensory Profile, a short little questionnaire with seven subscales.  We only have 245 participants, which I guess is a little small for LPA, but we were also collecting electrophysiological data on these participants and therefore couldn’t recruit too many people.  Could our small sample size be part of the problem?

If you have any insights, I’d really appreciate hearing them!

messages.author: 11f232522ba7c0f7
messages.subject: Re: Models could not be estimated error
parts:
Hi all,

I thought I would add some more information in case this helps you respond to my original question, which I know was rather vague!  But I played around some more and it seems like the issue is being largely caused by some specific subscales, the Low Energy/Weak subscale and also (to some extent) the Movement Sensitivity subscale.  When these subscales are not included, I am able to estimate a few profiles with varying variances.

The dataset I'm working with includes both autistic and neurotypical participants, and this the LEW and MS subscales have a somewhat peculiar pattern.  Most of the neurotypical participants have scores that are practically at ceiling, with rare exceptions, while there is a lot more variability among the autistic participants.

Does anyone have thoughts about how to resolve this situation?  Theoretically speaking, constraining the profiles to have equal variances when we know that two important populations have distinctly unequal variances seems quite problematic, but I also don't want to toss out these subscales and lose all the information in them!

Thanks so much.

messages.author: 3cfaef29dbc536f8
messages.subject: Re: Models could not be estimated error
parts:
Patrick, thank you for your message. I'm sorry for the delay. It is somewhat hard (for me) to say why the model may not converge, so I'll try not to speculate, but I think it basically suggests that the specification of the model isn't adequate for the parameters to be estimated. 

I understand what you mean regarding constraining the variances to be equal when your substantive knowledge indicates they shouldn't be. I would consider estimating that constrained model just to try to understand what is going on better: if it converges, it may well suggest that the model with varying variances is too complex (perhaps for this particular sample). 

Sorry it's hard to say more. I'm sorry for the delay, too. Do let us know if you have further questions - we'll try to answer more promptly going forward.
-Josh
